title: Blackbox optimization for origami-inspired bistable structures
contribution: Couples a validated compliant-crease FEM model of the waterbomb origami (Abaqus) with NOMAD/MADS to maximize bistability phi = dU/Umax under a stress limit, roughly doubling phi and showing how fixing a crash-driving variable, relaxing bounds and adding a Umax floor reshape the design (read from arXiv v1).
problem_entry: Application gap: fabricated bistable origami loses bistability, earlier optimization covered only beam structures or geometric incompatibility; DFO justified by a 30% simulation failure rate and ~110 s per successful call (pp. 1-2, 8-9).
key_idea: No new algorithm: 5 scaled design variables, symmetry-reduced two-step FEM (forming then actuation) as blackbox, NOMAD via PyNOMAD, stress-violating points discarded as failed evaluations (pp. 4-5, 8-9).
assumptions: Linear elastic S4 shells, Ef/Ec = 21.67; sigma_max below yield of face or crease; bounds from a 0.4 mm nozzle; n=4 and ri/ro=1/6 fixed; crashes tied to tall folds (large h/ro) (pp. 4-6, 8, 10).
proof_devices: none (application paper); modelling devices only: dimensionless bistability ratio phi = dU/Umax (p. 3)
1/2n sector with cyclic boundary conditions to cut FEM cost (p. 4)
energy from integrating reaction force over displacement (eq. 2, p. 7)
experiments: FEM validated on 3 contrasting designs vs 5 printed specimens each (Umax errors 5.5/2.9/25.7%, worst explained); 5 NOMAD runs of 1000 evaluations from Design I: phi 64.8% (30% fails), 58.4% with h/ro fixed (1% fails), 77.7%/76.8% with relaxed bounds (Umax collapse), 62.3% with Umax >= U0max; no seeds, repeats or competing solvers (pp. 6-11).
positioning: Placed in origami-engineering literature; DFO side cites only MADS/NOMAD/textbook/Alarie et al. 2021, Audet-Orban 2006, Chen-Kelley 2016; prior optimization described factually as limited in scope (pp. 2, 8).
writing: Physical-science style with author-contribution and data statements, gains as multiples ('two-fold'), MADS explained to engineers with a 2D poll picture (pp. 9-12).
limits_future: Future: bar-and-hinge surrogate, categorical material variable, curved creases, higher-resolution fabrication, multistable structures; code on GitHub (OriMads) but Abaqus-based and data on request (pp. 4, 12).

method_links.note: Hidden constraints (30% crashes) named; quantifiable stress constraint described as a discard/barrier, PB not discussed.
Code public and x0/final designs printed, but blackbox needs commercial Abaqus and data only on request.
Evaluation-count convergence plots, but single run per scenario, no seeds, no competing solver.
Run-diagnose-reformulate loop: fix h/ro to cut failures, relax active bounds, add Umax floor after degenerate optimum.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: 3 contrasting designs, 5 printed specimens each, per-design errors and a mechanism for the worst case

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: price a constraint by relaxing it
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: optimum on theta bounds -> rerun with relaxed bounds to show what finer fabrication buys (phi 77.7% vs 64.8%)

transferable: Justify DFO with measured failure rate and time per successful evaluation (pp. 8-9).
Fix the crash-driving variable and report both objective loss and failure-rate drop (p. 10).
After optimizing a ratio, audit numerator and denominator and add a floor constraint if the denominator collapses (p. 10).
Validate the simulator on deliberately contrasting designs, including a poor one, before optimizing (pp. 6-8).

quotes.text: In the present case, derivatives are difficult to obtain due to the numerous fails in the computation, therefore derivative-free optimization techniques [5] are required.
To reduce the number of failed evaluations, a second optimization is launched with the initial height fixed to h/ro = 0.6 along the process.

title: A novel sequential Benders-semidefinite framework with dual feasible proxy for multi-stage transmission expansion planning with contingencies
contribution: Integrates multistage TNEP+RPP with N-1 security in a generalized Benders loop over SDP-relaxed AC-OPF subproblems, accelerated by dual-feasible-proxy cuts, periodic exact Magnanti-Wong cuts and adaptive contingency screening, reporting e.g. 231.4 -> 38.9 min on IEEE-300.
problem_entry: TNEP and RPP solved separately, classical Benders gives weak/invalid cuts on nonconvex AC subproblems, and the authors' prior Benders-then-SDP paper lacked N-1 modelling and was dominated by SDP solve time (pp. 4-5).
key_idea: Any dual-feasible point of the SDP slave gives a valid cut: build one cheaply (K=3-5 IPM iterations or a small NN, then closed-form cone/PSD projection), use it when k mod r != 0 and solve exactly with MW strengthening otherwise (pp. 6-8).
assumptions: Binary investments; convex recourse via SDP relaxation; eps*tr(W) low-rank term asserted not to affect decisions; 'standard convex GBD assumptions' invoked but not listed (pp. 5-7).
proof_devices: informal validity argument: dual-feasible cuts never overestimate theta, so the master lower bound is nondecreasing (p. 7)
closed-form dual repair: max{0,.} for inequality duals, symmetrize and shift by lambda_min for the PSD block (p. 7)
Magnanti-Wong Pareto-optimal cut at core point xbar = alpha x^k + (1-alpha) xhat with ||g||_1 = 1 (pp. 7-8)
termination certified by full AC N-1 validation with re-entry on new violators (p. 8)
experiments: RTS-24, IEEE-118, IEEE-300, 3 stages; baselines are only ablations (BDSDP, +DFP, +Pareto); runtime/iterations, exact vs inexact SDP counts (548 -> 172 exact on IEEE-300), rank-1 rate 80.6%, 'final master gap' 5-12% vs a 0.1% stopping rule, zero N-1 violations; proxy training not described, promised MILP baseline absent (pp. 5-12).
positioning: Sorts rival families by weakness (heuristics, classical Benders, metaheuristics, monolithic multistage); credits Qiu-Tanneau-Van Hentenryck for the dual conic proxy; self-cites a PowerTech 2025 paper without Audet and Hydro-Quebec tools (pp. 4-5, 13-14).
writing: Numbered contributions, bold run-in labels ('Goal.', 'Key idea.'), adjectives in place of evidence, guarantees asserted without proof; abstract's exact-duals claim conflicts with Sec. 3.2 (pp. 3, 5, 7).
limits_future: No limitation stated; future work: renewable/demand uncertainty via stochastic or robust formulations (p. 13).

method_links.note: Cheap always-valid step (DFP cuts) plus scheduled exact step carrying convergence, transplanted to Benders; not shown robust to a poor cheap step.
Convergence claimed under unlisted 'standard convex GBD assumptions' with no proof; abstract says cuts always from exact duals while Sec. 3.2 uses inexact DFP cuts.
Only self-ablations in CPU minutes; promised MILP-based baseline missing; no variability reported.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: cheap valid bound + scheduled exact refresh
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: DFP cuts in most iterations, exact SDP + MW every r=3 iterations; Method 1 logic outside DFO in a paper Audet did not lead

transferable: Obtain a valid Benders cut without solving the slave: few IPM iterations, project duals onto the dual cone, evaluate the dual objective (p. 7).
Screen scenarios with a cheap relaxation, promote top-M violators, certify with the full model at termination and re-enter on new violators (p. 8).
Reject cuts whose violation is below a threshold (1e-5) to avoid numerically flat cuts (p. 7).
coauthors: E. Fathipasandideh, H. Supreme, H. Dagdougui, D. Asber

quotes.text: Any dual-feasible point of the slave SDP yields a valid lower bound and hence a valid Benders cut.
Optimality cuts are always derived from exact dual solutions, preserving convergence guarantees.

title: Benchmarking derivative-free optimization solvers for CSP plant design using the solar simulator
contribution: Shows how the public SOLAR suite can be used to choose a DFO solver and compares NOMAD, HEXALY, PRIMA (COBYLA) and CMA-ES on solar2/3/4/7/10 with data profiles, including constraint-violation profiles for infeasible starts.
problem_entry: Benchmark gap: realistic blackboxes are proprietary or hard to interface, so DFO solvers are benchmarked on problems that miss the field's difficulties; CSP design lacks standard benchmarks (pp. 3-4).
key_idea: A benchmarking procedure: select SOLAR problems by the property to test, form instances from LHS starting points (and seeds), run solvers with defaults and 100*n_p evaluations, compare with data profiles on f or on h (pp. 7-11).
assumptions: f, c valued in R U {inf}; a priori vs simulated constraints; artificial upper bound 1e5 for solvers needing bounds; linear constraints passed to HEXALY/PRIMA; replication, fidelity and seed settings of the runs not stated (pp. 4, 6-8).
proof_devices: tau-solved test (f0 - fN)/(f0 - f*) >= 1 - tau with kappa in groups of n_p+1 (p. 8)
constraint-violation data profile on h(x) = sum max{c_j,0}^2 (inf outside X) for infeasible starts (p. 11)
experiments: LHS census of 1e4 points per problem (a priori infeasible / simulated infeasible / feasible); 30 feasible starts for solar10 and solar7, 21 for solar2/3/4, 30 infeasible (a priori feasible) starts for solar3/4; feasibility counts show NOMAD 3/20 vs CMA-ES 5/20 on solar3 and NOMAD alone on solar4 (4/10); profile curves only in figures; no repeats or seeds reported (pp. 9-11).
positioning: SOLAR set against oversimplified analytic benchmarks; each competitor described with its home ground (smooth problems for HEXALY/PRIMA, noisy ill-conditioned for CMA-ES); methodology cited to More-Wild, Beiranvand-Hare-Lucet, Audet-Hare-Tribes (pp. 4, 8-9).
writing: Didactic figure pairing a data profile with instance convergence graphs; hedged results but strong discussion ('first freely available and open source suite', NOMAD 'reliably performs better'); NOMAD win read as evidence SOLAR is realistic; CMA-ES mislabelled model-based (pp. 8-12).
limits_future: Tuned parameters and larger budgets declared out of scope; smooth-problem claim untested; future is a hope that realistic benchmarks spread (pp. 11-12).

method_links.note: Use-case layer of a public artifact: versioned repo, selection guide, LHS starts, seeds, replication and fidelity parameters.
Evaluation currency, data profiles, four solver families incl. a commercial one, defaults, h-profiles for infeasible starts.
Competitors' smooth home ground described but not tested; seeds/replications not reported.
A priori vs simulated constraints drive the LHS census and the choice of infeasible starts that let the simulator run.
Benchmark built by NOMAD developers and NOMAD's win used as evidence of realism (single-codebase bias).

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: 1e4 LHS points per problem tabulated as a priori infeasible / simulated infeasible / feasible to grade difficulty and draw starts
a priori constraints checked by the solar code, simulation skipped when violated

transferable: Run an LHS census and publish the three-way feasibility table before benchmarking (p. 9).
Draw infeasible starts that satisfy the cheap constraints so the simulator is exercised (p. 10).
Use h-based data profiles when f-based ones are uninformative (p. 11).
Pair a data profile with the per-instance convergence plots behind it (Fig. 4, p. 9).
Publish a guide mapping solver requirements to benchmark instances (p. 7).
coauthors: X. Lebeuf, S. Le Digabel, P. Brillon, M. Diago, C. Tribes

quotes.text: As a result, DFO solvers are too often benchmarked on problems that do not fully capture the challenges of the field.
This is a sign that solar successfully captures the difficulties encountered with real BBO problems.

title: Optimal sorting with comparisons involving three elements
contribution: Introduces worst-case sorting with three-element comparisons and gives constructive upper bounds t_n for n <= 1000 as the minimum of six lemma-backed heuristics, with hand-built certificates for n = 13 (16 comparisons) and n = 21 (34).
problem_entry: Change the oracle of the classical minimum-comparison sorting problem from pairwise (2 outcomes) to three-way (6 outcomes); the counting bound ceil(log6 n!) seems tight only for n = 3 (p. 4).
key_idea: Portfolio recurrence t_n = min{s_n, p_n, f_n, v_n, m_n, g_n}, where chain-based heuristics enumerate group partitions and add merge costs from Theorem 2.2, computed bottom-up (pp. 5-8).
assumptions: Distinct reals; each comparison returns the full order of three elements; worst-case only (p. 4).
proof_devices: induction on n for two chains plus a v-chain sorted in n-2 comparisons (Thm 2.2(i), pp. 4-5)
reduction of (ii)/(iii) to (i) after one or two comparisons with a case split on a singleton (p. 5)
pivot-based case analysis by number of elements on each side, closed by Thm 2.2, with symmetry halving the cases (Props 3.1-3.2, pp. 8-11)
experiments: Table of alpha_n, beta_n, six heuristic values, lower bound and t_n for n <= 40 and n in {50,100,200,500,1000}, with best/unique-best marking and accounting rows (f best for all 23 <= n <= 1000); gap t_n - l_n grows to 1053 at n = 1000 (pp. 11-12).
positioning: Builds on the pairwise minimum-comparison literature (Ford-Johnson, Peczarski, Cheng et al.) and on the author's own 2014 three-tray-balance paper; claims a new class of problems (pp. 4, 12).
writing: Short proof-driven paper with named heuristics and pseudo-code; abstract claims 'optimal or near-optimal' while the discussion says many t_n are likely not optimal; typo 14 for 13 in Prop. 3.1's proof (pp. 3, 9, 12).
limits_future: Only n = 6-15 studied in detail, enumeration impractical from n = 9, optimality unconfirmed; future: prove or disprove optimality, generalize to p-way comparisons (pp. 12-13).

method_links.note: Every upper bound has a constructive proof and the discussion admits optimality is unproven, but no tightness beyond n = 3 and the abstract overstates ('optimal or near-optimal').

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: six lemma-backed constructions enumerated over partitions, pointwise minimum computed bottom-up, with accounting rows of which construction wins
2014 15-marble puzzle generalized to all n <= 1000 with an open p-way extension

transferable: Print the information-theoretic lower bound as a column next to your upper bounds (p. 12).
Turn structural finishing lemmas into heuristics by enumerating partitions and combining by pointwise minimum (pp. 7-8).
Add accounting rows (times best, uniquely best, largest instance where best) to a best-of-k table (p. 12).
Use symmetry to halve pivot-based case analyses (pp. 8-9).

quotes.text: We report optimal or near-optimal results for all values up to n = 40 elements, and for selected instances up to n = 1000.
Larger instances have not been studied as thoroughly, and many of the reported values of tn are likely not optimal.

title: Micro-PRIAD: A power utility simulator for blackbox optimization benchmarking
contribution: Releases Micro-PRIAD, an open-source Julia simulator with ten stochastic Monte Carlo blackbox instances (nine constrained, realistic power-grid maintenance problems plus one fast unconstrained one) that mimics Hydro-Quebec's PRIAD blackbox, including intermediate outputs with solver-side interrupters and sub-sampling hooks.
problem_entry: Realistic BBO benchmarks are scarce and single-instance, analytic suites lack real difficulties; Hydro-Quebec's PRIAD blackbox needs up to 145 days per evaluation (pp. 4-5).
key_idea: Build a scaled-down public twin: keep the block structure (degradation, grid generation, MC unavailability simulator in eta groups of s draws, cost block), drop power flow, expose interrupters, a subsampler and a fidelity parameter to the solver (pp. 6-7, 16-18).
assumptions: Geometric failures, uniform failure times, lognormal repair/maintenance times (variance 0.25), analytic degradation curves, static outage prices; constraints classified QRAK/QRSK and rescaled to [-500, .] with threshold 0; seed fixes all randomness (pp. 10-15).
proof_devices: horn plot: 100 evaluations at x_best per N, choose smallest N with 3*sigma/mean <= 0.1% (N = 1e4) (pp. 13-14)
second vector of per-component sample counts N_i returned with each intermediate output (p. 18)
linear fidelity map, 1e-4 fidelity = one MC draw (p. 29)
experiments: 2D slices on 200x200 grids at N = 500 (>10 h each) and at N = 1..1e4 (a week for 1e4); 1D cuts showing feasibility flips at low N; 32 instances, five anonymized solvers, 32 h budgets, tau = 0.005, data profiles vs n+1 evaluation groups and vs hours (rank shifts explained by sampled regions), and a same-solver comparison with a static surrogate (N = 1e3, 10 calls = 1 evaluation) (pp. 19-22).
positioning: Against analytic suites (CUTEst, BBOB) and single-instance realistic problems (STYRENE, wing, groundwater); credits SOLAR as the only collection covering both gaps; novelty hedged 'to the author’s knowledge' (pp. 4-5).
writing: Twofold contributions, honest about features kept only 'to mimic' PRIAD, a third of the report is a user guide; overreaching inference from the surrogate test to intermediate outputs; several default/name inconsistencies between Sec. 3 and the guide (pp. 5, 17-31).
limits_future: Limits given as simplifications (no power flow, analytic degradation, static prices, negligible sub-sampling gain); results called illustrative; no future work stated (pp. 3, 6, 10, 12, 18, 22).

method_links.note: Executable with x.txt input and one-line output, constraint classification, seeds, fidelity, multiple instances, open code and user guide.
Starting points and best-known values are not printed (x_best used but not given).
Le Digabel-Wild labels per constraint; deterministic a priori constraints available via -N 0 and a deterministic-info interrupter.
Profiles on evaluations and on time, surrogate calls charged at cost ratio, seeds in instance definition.
Benchmark co-designed with the group's intermediate-output algorithms (Inter-DS, multi-fidelity constraints) and evaluated with RunnerPost.
